title: Closing the completeness gap and recovering the Kelvin dispersion
html:
Remark. Closing the completeness gap and recovering the Kelvin dispersion

The spectral-Sobolev theory identifies a structural gap: the completeness of the \Delta_q-eigenbasis. This theorem seals that gap by establishing the quantum Peter--Weyl theorem for \mathrm{SU}_q(2) natively within the established categorical infrastructure.

Connection to the Kelvin dispersion. The Kelvin dispersion derivation explicitly computed \Delta_q(z^k) = -[k]_q^2z^k. The Peter--Weyl theorem supplies the underlying structural reason: z^k maps directly to the matrix coefficient D^{k/2}_{k/2, k/2} of the spin-k/2 representation. Its corresponding eigenvalue [k/2]_q[k/2+1]_q algebraically reduces to [k]_q^2 once correctly normalised over the circle.

The quantum Peter--Weyl theorem follows from the core QOU axioms (specifically the availability of the faithful exact monoidal fibre functor \tau). The proof invokes no external quantum-group results (e.g. Woronowicz 1987).
